oil.summary: Crude sold off sharply today — WTI -3.79% to $80.11 and Brent -3.50% to $85.91 — as both OPEC and the IEA slashed their 2026 demand outlooks, overwhelming the geopolitical risk premium that had lifted prices nearly 4-5% over the prior week. RBOB gasoline cratered 9.59% to $2.8532/gal, the standout mover, while heating oil held up best at -1.74% ($4.2291/gal) amid a deepening global diesel supply crunch tied to Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries and a Houthi attack on a Saudi refining facility. A partial diplomatic easing emerged after Ukraine reportedly halted tanker strikes at a Russian port following a U.S. Vice Presidential request, though refinery attacks continued. Russia's energy sector is under enough strain that it is now importing gasoline from India for the first time. Three tankers damaged in the Gulf and stalled U.S.-Iran talks keep tail risks elevated.
drivers: OPEC and IEA both cut 2026 demand forecasts, triggering today's broad crude selloff
Ongoing Ukrainian and Houthi refinery strikes sustain diesel supply crunch; Russia forced to import gasoline from India
U.S.-Iran conflict escalation (three tankers damaged in Gulf, Hormuz concerns) provides a floor, but ceasefire signals on tanker strikes capped upside
sources: The Hague Centre for Strategic Studies

gas.summary: European and U.S. gas markets diverged sharply today. TTF surged 3.89% to €61.021/MWh, extending a remarkable +16.44% weekly and +15.22% monthly rally driven by the U.S.-Iran war disrupting global LNG supply chains and elevating risk premiums on cargoes serving Europe and Asia. Henry Hub slipped 2.28% to $2.74/MMBtu, remaining pressured on a one-month basis (-6.29%), reflecting ample domestic U.S. supply. On infrastructure, an Alaska LNG pipeline bill failed to pass the state legislature, prompting a sharp gubernatorial rebuke, removing a potential future export avenue. South Korean private equity firm Hahn & Co is consolidating SK Shipping and H-Line Shipping to create Asia's largest LNG carrier operator, signalling continued long-term institutional confidence in LNG trade growth.
drivers: U.S.-Iran conflict driving TTF sharply higher (+16.4% on the week) as LNG supply disruption fears grip European and Asian buyers
Henry Hub under pressure on a monthly basis despite a modest weekly bounce, reflecting U.S. domestic supply fundamentals decoupled from geopolitics
Alaska LNG pipeline bill failure removes a near-term U.S. export capacity catalyst; South Korean LNG fleet consolidation signals sustained Asian import demand

power.summary: The power and carbon complex is being shaped primarily by the knock-on effects of the broader energy crisis rather than standalone power-sector news today. EU carbon EUAs nudged up 0.38% to $78.21/EUA, continuing a modest but steady monthly grind higher (+2.10%), partly supported by elevated TTF gas prices (+3.89% today) which raise the cost of gas-fired generation and indirectly support carbon values. India is emerging as a major structural theme: the country is now the world's largest proposed new coal power capacity builder with 638 million metric tons of annual new capacity planned, while separately expanding strategic petroleum reserves. In China, elevated crude prices are delivering record profits to coal-to-chemicals producers. A MIT-linked framework targeting nuclear fusion financing drew attention on the longer-dated clean energy horizon, but headline news flow for the EU power market specifically is thin today.
drivers: Surging TTF gas prices support EU EUA values by raising gas-fired generation costs across the continent
India accelerating coal power expansion and strategic reserve build, signalling medium-term fossil demand pressure on global carbon markets
China's coal-to-chemicals sector reporting record profits as high crude prices boost coal-derived product competitiveness
